blocks.text: The Hebrew words of Isaiah, ואסף שללכם אסף החסיל, your spoil shall be gathered with the gathering of the locust, can be referred to the locusts in either an active or a passive sense. In the former sense it will be a gathering of the locusts if these animals scrape off whatever they meet and strip it for their own use; in the latter it is the gathering of the locusts themselves, as they consume the crops, which is done by the farmers, who collect them in vessels or push them in heaps into ditches and pits to kill them. Forerius, a Spaniard by birth, observes on the passage of Isaiah that this is done in Africa and Spain. Cf. Io. Leonh. Frisch, Beschreibung von allerley Insecten (Berlin 1750), vol. 9, p. 9, and Gleditsch, Abhandlung von Vertilgung der Zugkeuschrecken, Berlin 1752, p. 59. Jerome took the same view, rendering the whole sentence thus: and your spoils shall be gathered together, as the bruchus is collected, as when the ditches have been filled with it. Ludov. Cappellus set out this sense more explicitly: this expression, he says, is taken from country people, who collect in heaps the bruchi and locusts that harm the crops, and trample them underfoot once collected. So the prophet means this: the Jews will easily and with no trouble, with no one hindering them, plunder your spoils from the camp, gather them together, and carry them off with them. Doederlein followed the same sense in his version of this passage, and Paulus in his Clavis. But this interpretation is flatly contradicted by the second member, in which the locusts are introduced as being in action and motion, כמשק גבים שקק בו, running to and fro like the running to and fro of locusts, namely he runs to and fro, i.e. there is running to and fro in it. The sense of these words can scarcely be other than this: that the Israelites will gather the spoils of the fallen enemies, scattered over the fields, like locusts, and will run to and fro, leaping in the manner of those same locusts, as they gather them. Hence it is clear, from the law of the parallelism of members, that the gathering of the locusts in the first member is a gathering done by the locusts. Grotius also saw this, writing on this passage: „your spoils shall be gathered together, as the bruchus gathers, they will be gathered from you, the Assyrians, with as much impunity as the bruchus grazes on the plants. What follows in the Hebrew demands this interpretation.“ The prophet elegantly used the verb אסף, which is properly used of the gathering of crops and produce that takes place at harvest time. This the locusts do when in great swarms they settle on the fields and consume them.
